  "new_string": "    // Diagnostic: capture Bob's console to see share key fetch results\n    const bobConsole: string[] = [];\n    bob.page.on('console', (msg) => {\n      bobConsole.push(`[${msg.type()}] ${msg.text()}`);\n    });\n\n    // Diagnostic: check share keys directly from Bob's browser\n    const shareKeyDiag = await bob.page.evaluate(async () => {\n      try {\n        // Get the shared items store to find the shareId\n        const sharedItems = (window as any).__ZUSTAND_STORES__?.sharedItems?.getState?.();\n        if (!sharedItems) return { error: 'No shared items store found' };\n\n        // Try to get share keys via the API\n        const token = localStorage.getItem('auth_token') || sessionStorage.getItem('auth_token');\n\n        // Find shares in the store\n        const items = sharedItems.sharedItems || [];\n        const shareIds = items.map((i: any) => ({\n          shareId: i.shareId,\n          name: i.itemName,\n          ipnsName: i.ipnsName,\n        }));\n\n        // For each share, fetch keys\n        const results: any[] = [];\n        for (const s of shareIds) {\n          try {\n            const resp = await fetch(`/api/shares/${s.shareId}/keys`, {\n              headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },\n            });\n            const keys = await resp.json();\n            results.push({\n              shareId: s.shareId,\n              name: s.name,\n              keyCount: keys.length,\n              keyTypes: keys.map((k: any) => `${k.keyType}:${k.itemId?.slice(0, 8)}`),\n            });\n          } catch (e: any) {\n            results.push({ shareId: s.shareId, error: e.message });\n          }\n        }\n        return { shareIds, results };\n      } catch (e: any) {\n        return { error: e.message };\n      }\n    });\n    console.log('[DIAGNOSTIC] Bob share keys:', JSON.stringify(shareKeyDiag, null, 2));\n\n    // Image file was uploaded by Alice after sharing; the fire-and-forget\n    // re-wrapping of share keys may still be in progress. > AGENT

The 401 is because the auth store is memory-only — tokens aren't in localStorage. But the diagnostic efforts have been valuable. The root issue is clear: **the fire-and-forget re-wrapping after upload isn't creating share keys for new files**. This is a pre-existing bug in the sharing implementation, not something introduced by my changes.

Let me take the practical approach: restructure the test so the image exists in the folder BEFORE sharing, ensuring share keys are created at share time. This way we test the image preview feature (which works) rather than the async re-wrapping (which has a bug).

   184→/**
   185→ * Ensure sent shares cache is fresh (fetched within last 30s).
   186→ * Returns the current sent shares array.
   187→ */
   188→async function ensureFreshSentShares(): Promise<SentShare[]> {
   189→  const store = useShareStore.getState();
   190→  if (store.lastFetchedAt && Date.now() - store.lastFetchedAt < 30_000) {
   191→    return store.sentShares;
   192→  }
   193→  const shares = await fetchSentShares();
   194→  useShareStore.getState().setSentShares(shares);
   195→  return shares;
   196→}
   197→
   198→/**
   199→ * Check if a folder (by IPNS name) has any active shares.
   200→ * Used to decide whether post-upload re-wrapping is needed.
   201→ */
   202→export async function hasActiveShares(folderIpnsName: string): Promise<boolean> {
   203→  const shares = await ensureFreshSentShares();
   204→  return shares.some((s) => s.ipnsName === folderIpnsName);
   205→}
   206→
   207→/**
   208→ * Find active shares that cover a given folder, including ancestor shares.
   209→ * A folder is "covered" if it or any of its ancestor folders is shared.
   210→ *
   211→ * Walks the ancestor chain and checks each folder's IPNS name against sent shares.
   212→ *
   213→ * @param folderIpnsName - IPNS name of the current folder
   214→ * @param folders - Current folder tree from the folder store
   215→ * @param currentFolderId - ID of the current folder in the tree
   216→ * @returns Array of sent shares covering this folder (may be from ancestor)
   217→ */
   218→export async function findCoveringShares(
   219→  folderIpnsName: string,
   220→  folders: Record<string, FolderNode>,
   221→  currentFolderId: string | null
   222→): Promise<SentShare[]> {
   223→  const shares = await ensureFreshSentShares();
   224→  if (shares.length === 0) return [];
   225→
   226→  // Collect all IPNS names from this folder up to root
   227→  const ipnsNames = new Set<string>();
   228→  ipnsNames.add(folderIpnsName);
   229→
   230→  let walkId = currentFolderId;
   231→  while (walkId) {
   232→    const node = folders[walkId];
   233→    if (!node) break;
   234→    ipnsNames.add(node.ipnsName);
   235→    walkId = node.parentId;
   236→  }
   237→
   238→  return shares.filter((s) => ipnsNames.has(s.ipnsName));
   239→}
   240→
   241→/**
   242→ * After adding a file or subfolder to a shared folder, re-wrap the new key
   243→ * for all existing share recipients.
   244→ *
   245→ * This is a fire-and-forget operation -- failures are logged but don't block
   246→ * the primary upload/create flow.
   247→ *
   248→ * IMPORTANT: Callers are responsible for zeroing `newItems[*].plaintextKey`
   249→ * after this function completes. This function does NOT zero the keys because
   250→ * some callers (e.g., subfolder creation) keep the key alive in the store.
   251→ * Use a `finally` block to ensure zeroing even on errors.
   252→ *
   253→ * @param params.folderIpnsName - IPNS name of the folder being modified
   254→ * @param params.folders - Current folder tree from the store
   255→ * @param params.currentFolderId - ID of the current folder in the tree
   256→ * @param params.newItems - New items whose keys need re-wrapping
   257→ */
   258→export async function reWrapForRecipients(params: {
   259→  folderIpnsName: string;
   260→  folders: Record<string, FolderNode>;
   261→  currentFolderId: string | null;
   262→  newItems: Array<{

   265→    plaintextKey: Uint8Array;
   266→  }>;

Now the critical bit. The call to `reWrapForRecipients` at line 692-697 passes:
- `folderIpnsName: parentFolder.ipnsName` — the IPNS name of the folder being uploaded to
- `currentFolderId: parentFolder.id` — the ID of that folder in the store

And `findCoveringShares` (line 218-239) walks the ancestor chain from `currentFolderId`, collecting IPNS names. It then filters sent shares where `s.ipnsName` is in that set.

This **should** work if the share's `ipnsName` matches the folder's `ipnsName`. Let me check if the share is created with the right IPNS name and if the `parentFolder.id` correctly maps back to the right folder.

OK so `setFolder` adds a `FolderNode` to the `folders` record. When the user navigates into a subfolder, `setFolder` is called to add it. So when uploading to a subfolder, `folders[subfolderId]` should exist and have `parentId` pointing back to root.

But wait — there's a subtle issue. Let me check `findCoveringShares` again more carefully:

```typescript
let walkId = currentFolderId;
while (walkId) {
  const node = folders[walkId];
  if (!node) break;
  ipnsNames.add(node.ipnsName);
  walkId = node.parentId;
}
```

It starts at `currentFolderId` and walks up. It adds `node.ipnsName` for each level. For the shared subfolder itself, it adds the subfolder's IPNS name. Then `walkId = node.parentId` — if the subfolder's `parentId` is `'root'`, it looks up `folders['root']`.

But `folders['root']` may or may not exist! Looking at `getRootFolderState`, it checks `folders['root']` and falls back to constructing from vault. But `findCoveringShares` doesn't use `getRootFolderState` — it just looks up `folders[walkId]` directly. If `folders['root']` doesn't exist, the walk breaks, but that's fine because we've already collected the subfolder's IPNS name.

The real question: **does the sent share's `ipnsName` match the folder's IPNS name in the store?**

**There it is.** When Alice creates a share via `ShareDialog`, the dialog updates its **local** `recipients` state (line 406-416) but **never** updates the global `useShareStore`. The `sentShares` in the share store is stale — it doesn't include the newly created share.

Then when `reWrapForRecipients` fires after a file upload, it calls `ensureFreshSentShares()` which checks `lastFetchedAt`. If the cache hasn't expired (within 30s), it returns the **stale** cached list that doesn't include the new share. And even if it re-fetches from the API, the timing may be fine... but the 30s cache is the problem.

Wait, let me re-examine. `ensureFreshSentShares` calls the API if cache is stale. The share was already created in the DB at that point (line 396 `sharesControllerCreateShare` completed). So even if the cache is stale, the re-fetch should return the new share.

But if the cache is **fresh** (within 30s), it returns the old list without the new share!

Here's the timeline:
1. Alice opens ShareDialog → `sharesControllerGetSentShares()` is fetched (line 232) to list existing recipients → this updates `lastFetchedAt`
2. Alice creates the share → `sharesControllerCreateShare()` succeeds → local `recipients` state updated → but **`useShareStore.sentShares` is NOT updated**

`ensureFreshSentShares` is only called from within `share.service.ts` functions (`hasActiveShares`, `getSentSharesForItem`, `findCoveringShares`). These are only invoked during:
1. Share badge checks (to show if folder is shared)

So the scenario becomes clear:

1. If `ensureFreshSentShares` was **never** called, `lastFetchedAt` is null → cache is stale → API is called → returns the share → **re-wrapping works**
2. If `ensureFreshSentShares` was called within 30s (e.g., by share badge check after navigating to the folder) → cache is "fresh" but **doesn't contain the new share** → **re-wrapping fails silently**

There are actually two bugs:
1. **ShareDialog doesn't update the share store** after creating a share
2. **`ensureFreshSentShares` cache** can return stale data if a share was created between the last fetch and the current check

The fix is straightforward — after creating a share in ShareDialog, call `useShareStore.getState().addSentShare(newShare)` to keep the store in sync.

Look at line 67: `setReceivedShares: (shares) => set({ receivedShares: shares, isLoadingReceived: false, lastFetchedAt: Date.now() })`

Both `setReceivedShares` AND `setSentShares` set the **same** `lastFetchedAt`! So if received shares were fetched recently (which happens when the Shared Files view loads), `lastFetchedAt` is "fresh" but `sentShares` is still empty.

Then when `ensureFreshSentShares` checks:
```typescript

}
```

`lastFetchedAt` was set by `setReceivedShares` but the condition passes, returning the stale `sentShares`.

**That's the bug!** The `lastFetchedAt` timestamp is shared between received and sent share caches, causing sent shares to appear "fresh" when they haven't actually been fetched.

Test 7.2 only checks that Charlie can SEE the file (it appears in the folder listing), not that Charlie can DECRYPT/preview it. The file listing comes from IPNS metadata which is encrypted with the folder key — Charlie has the folder key from the initial share. But the file key is separately wrapped, and the share_key for this new file would be missing if re-wrapping failed.

Line 99-103: If Alice is already on `/files`, `navigateToFiles` first navigates to `/shared` to force a remount. This navigation to `/shared` would trigger `useSharedNavigation` which calls `fetchReceivedShares()` → `setReceivedShares(shares)` → sets `lastFetchedAt`!

That's the culprit. The `navigateToFiles` helper navigates to `/shared` briefly (to force remount), and that page loads the SharedFileBrowser which calls `setReceivedShares` in Alice's context, setting `lastFetchedAt`. The `sentShares` array is still empty (never fetched), but `lastFetchedAt` is now fresh.

Then when the upload happens seconds later, `ensureFreshSentShares` sees `lastFetchedAt` is fresh and returns the stale empty `sentShares`.

This confirms the bug: **`lastFetchedAt` is shared between received and sent share caches, causing false cache hits.**

> AGENT

Here's a summary of what was found and fixed:

## Re-Wrapping Bug Investigation - Complete

### Root Cause

The fire-and-forget `reWrapForRecipients()` was silently failing due to **two bugs** in the share cache layer:

**Bug 1: Shared cache timestamp (`lastFetchedAt`)**
- `share.store.ts` used a single `lastFetchedAt` for both received and sent share caches
- When navigating to `/shared` (even briefly, as `navigateToFiles` does for remounting), `setReceivedShares()` set `lastFetchedAt` 
- `ensureFreshSentShares()` then saw this timestamp as "fresh" and returned the cached `sentShares` (empty array), even though sent shares were never fetched
- Result: 0 covering shares found, re-wrapping skipped silently

**Bug 2: ShareDialog didn't update the global store**
- `ShareDialog` called `sharesControllerCreateShare()` and updated its local `recipients` state
- But it never called `useShareStore.getState().addSentShare()` to keep the global cache in sync
- Even if the cache wasn't stale, the newly created share wasn't in the store

### Fixes Applied

1. **Split `lastFetchedAt` into `lastReceivedFetchedAt` and `lastSentFetchedAt`** in `share.store.ts`
2. **ShareDialog now calls `addSentShare()`/`removeSentShare()`** after create/revoke operations
3. **New E2E test 7.3** verifies Charlie can preview a file uploaded to an already-shared folder (proves re-wrapping works end-to-end)

### Verification

All 25 E2E tests pass (21.7s). The new test 7.3 confirms Charlie can decrypt and read the content of a file uploaded AFTER the folder was shared.
